newsitem.title: TURKEY: Another Turk anti-Islamist MP quits Ciller party.
newsitem.headline: Another Turk anti-Islamist MP quits Ciller party.

text.p: An anti-Islamist Turkish MP said on Thursday she had quit Tansu Ciller's True Path Party, in a resignation that boosts secularist Mesut Yilmaz's effort to set up a coalition.
"Everyone must play a role in protecting the secular, democratic state at this time," deputy Isilay Saygin said in a written statement.
She was the third MP to abandon Ciller since rival Yilmaz was made prime minister-designate last Friday.
Main opposition leader Yilmaz is relying on defections from Ciller's faction to win a vote of confidence in any government he sets up.
He needs to lure at least another six deputies from a pro-Islamic alliance led by Ciller into his camp and guarantee the support of 16 independents, most of whom favour him.
Yilmaz is trying to establish a coalition that would freeze out the Islamists of Necmettin Erbakan, who resigned as prime minister last week after months of army pressure.
Saygin was one of two True Path MPs who refused to sign a document this week to pledge she would not vote for Yilmaz.
Yilmaz began a second round of talks with leftist leader Bulent Ecevit on Thursday on forming the coalition. Ecevit, an avowed secularist, is tipped for a cabinet post in the planned government.
